settings.title: Dry-fit first
settings.body: Check KRYO, hose, Halo, power and refill reach before sticking the rail.

settings.title: Keep airflow and power clear
settings.body: Keep rear airflow open. PSU, mains plug and outlet stay dry and away from splash.

settings.title: Check every seal
settings.body: Rubber seals sit flat inside the fittings. Hand-tighten only.

settings.title: Prime before power
settings.body: Never run the pump dry. Do not overfill and never set KRYO below 1°C.

settings.title: Back first
settings.body: For the first session, start with the water across the upper back and shoulders, not the face or chest.

settings.definition: The ring-shaped shower head that mounts on the rail above you. It spreads cold water across the shoulders and upper body.
The control on the Halo that opens and closes water flow. Keep it closed until you are ready to start.
The vertical adhesive rail that fixes to the wall and carries the Halo.
The height-adjustable carrier that slides inside the rail and holds the Halo.
Carries water between KRYO and the Halo. A rubber seal sits inside each fitting.
The power supply that converts the UAE wall supply to 24V DC for KRYO. It must stay dry.
The opening on top of KRYO where you add water, and the plug that closes it.
The control on KRYO that starts and stops circulation to the Halo.

settings.title: Position & plan
settings.purpose: Decide where everything goes before mounting anything.
settings.critical: Do not stick the rail down until the complete layout has been checked.
settings.detail:
Fully dry-fit KRYO, the hose, the Halo, the rail, the power supply and refill access before mounting anything.

The Halo must sit a minimum of 30 cm above the tallest user’s head. Where the room and hose allow, 40–50 cm is preferred.

A higher Halo improves the spread of water across the shoulders and upper body.

Check every component before you begin. Do not install KRYO if anything is missing or damaged:

  • KRYO
  • Two-metre hose
  • Halo with flow adjuster
  • Rubber seals
  • UAE PSU and plug
  • Fill-opening plug
  • Mounting rail
  • Sliding connector
  • Phillips-head screwdriver

The rubber seals are small but essential — keep them with the hose fittings.

Reach checks. Connect the hose and Halo, hold the rail in the proposed position, then confirm the hose reaches without pulling or kinking, the PSU reaches a suitable wall outlet, and a bidet or shower hose can reach the fill opening.
settings.alt_1: KRYO upright on a level floor with the rear airflow area kept clear

settings.text: Place KRYO upright on a stable, level floor.
settings.detail: KRYO must stay upright. A level floor keeps the internal water level readable and stops the unit rocking while the pump runs.

settings.text: Keep the vents and airflow area clear.
settings.detail: Warm air exits from the rear. Pressing KRYO against a wall, towel or curtain restricts airflow, which can reduce cooling performance and may cause overheating.

settings.text: Check the hose reaches without pulling or kinking.
settings.detail: Hold the rail where you plan to mount it and run the hose along its intended path before anything is fixed.
settings.image_alt: Planning where KRYO, the hose, the Halo and the power supply will sit before mounting anything

settings.text: Check the power reaches and refill access works.
settings.detail: The PSU must reach a suitable mains outlet, and a bidet or shower hose must reach the fill opening.

settings.text: Plan the Halo height above the tallest user.
settings.detail:
The Halo must sit a minimum of 30 cm above the tallest user’s head. Where the room and hose allow, 40–50 cm is preferred.

A higher Halo improves the spread of water across the shoulders and upper body.
settings.image_alt: Halo height guide showing 30 cm minimum and 40 to 50 cm preferred above the tallest user's head

settings.text: Face the spray away from the display and power side.
settings.detail: KRYO’s display and power button are on its right-hand side. Mount the Halo on the opposite side where possible.

settings.text: Do not remove the rail adhesive yet.
settings.detail: The adhesive is difficult to reposition. Leave the backing on until the complete layout has been checked.

settings.title: Mount the Halo
settings.purpose: Assemble the rail and mount it once the position is confirmed.
settings.critical: Confirm the final location before applying the adhesive.
settings.detail:
The wall must be smooth, clean and completely dry, and free from soap film, oil, dust or loose material. Use only the preparation method approved for your wall and the supplied adhesive.

Remove one rail end cap, insert the sliding connector, confirm the slider moves freely, then refit the end cap and tighten the screw without overtightening.

Align the rail carefully, then press firmly and evenly across every adhesive point.

The adhesive is difficult to reposition once it has made contact.

Use the adjustment control to move the Halo height on the rail, and confirm the Halo is secure after any adjustment.

Final position test. Fit the Halo and hose to the slider, hold the complete rail against the wall and check once more:

  • The rail is vertical
  • The Halo is high enough
  • The hose is not stretched
  • The hose has no sharp kink
  • Spray points away from the power side
  • Rear airflow stays clear
  • The refill hose reaches KRYO
  • The power cable reaches safely

Mark the rail position with removable tape.
settings.alt_1: Pressing the mounting rail firmly and evenly onto the prepared wall

settings.text: Clean and completely dry the wall.
settings.detail: The wall must be smooth, clean and completely dry, and free from soap film, oil, dust or loose material.

settings.text: Remove one rail end cap and insert the sliding connector.
settings.detail: Use the supplied screwdriver, then slide the height-adjustable connector into the rail.

settings.text: Confirm the slider moves, then refit the end cap.
settings.detail: Press the button and check the connector moves freely along the rail before anything goes on the wall. Tighten the end-cap screw without overtightening.

settings.text: Align the rail carefully.
settings.detail: Mark the position with removable tape first. The adhesive is difficult to reposition.

settings.text: Press firmly and evenly into position.
settings.detail: Make first contact carefully, then press across every adhesive point.

settings.text: Adjust the Halo height and confirm it is secure.
settings.detail: Use the adjustment control to move the Halo up or down the rail, then check it is secure before use.
settings.image_alt: Using the adjustment control to move the Halo up or down on the rail

settings.title: Connect
settings.purpose: Connect the Halo, hose and power.
settings.critical:
Seal flat. Fit squarely. Hand-tight only.

Keep the PSU, mains plug and outlet dry.
settings.detail:
A rubber seal sits inside each threaded fitting. It must be flat — never missing, twisted or pinched. A missing or misaligned seal is the most common cause of leaking.

Start the threads square, then hand-tighten only. Do not cross-thread and do not overtighten.

Keep KRYO’s water-flow control and the Halo flow adjuster closed initially.

Connect KRYO’s 24V DC lead to the supplied PSU, then connect the PSU to a suitable mains outlet.

The PSU, plug and mains connection must stay dry and away from splash and standing water. Route cables away from water and foot traffic, and dry your hands before handling power.
settings.alt_1: Attaching the hose to the Halo flow adjuster, hand-tight only

settings.text: Check the rubber seal inside each threaded fitting.
settings.detail: The seal must sit flat inside the fitting. Missing, twisted or pinched seals are the most common cause of leaks.

settings.text: Connect the hose to the Halo flow adjuster.
settings.detail: Start the threads square, then hand-tighten only. Do not cross-thread and do not overtighten.

settings.text: Connect the other end to the KRYO cooling unit.
settings.detail: Check the hose then follows a smooth path with no sharp kink.
settings.image_alt: Attaching the other end of the hose to the KRYO cooling unit outlet

settings.text: Keep both flow controls closed to start.
settings.detail: Leave KRYO’s water-flow control and the Halo flow adjuster closed until you are ready to prime.

settings.text: Connect the 24V DC lead to the PSU, then the PSU to a mains outlet.
settings.detail: Keep KRYO switched off and dry your hands first. Place the PSU and its connection outside the splash zone and route cables away from water and foot traffic.
settings.image_alt: Connecting the PSU to a suitable dry mains outlet away from splash

settings.title: Fill & start
settings.purpose: Prime KRYO, start circulation and fill it safely.
settings.critical:
If you hear a harsh dry-running sound or water is not circulating: switch KRYO off immediately, add water, and restart only once adequately primed.

Never set below 1°C. Never allow the reservoir to freeze.
settings.detail:
Water must be added before the pump is operated. Running the pump dry can damage it.

Keep both flow controls closed until KRYO is running and circulating normally.

Switch KRYO on, confirm the internal light turns on, and listen for smooth internal circulation.

Keep the internal light on while filling so you can see the level clearly. Fill slowly and stop below the upper internal and electrical area. Do not overfill.

Dry the top surface before refitting the fill plug, and confirm the plug sits correctly.

Set approximately 15°C for first use, then lower the temperature gradually only once you know how your body responds.

The exact minimum priming volume and the exact maximum fill level are pending confirmation and are not published here.
settings.alt_1: Opening the fill plug on top of KRYO to add water
settings.alt_2: Switching KRYO on once water has been added
settings.always_visible: You may hear the internal pressurising pump while KRYO is operating. This is normal.

settings.text: Open the fill plug.
settings.detail: Unscrew the plug on top of KRYO by hand. No tools are required.

settings.text: Add water before operating the pump.
settings.detail: The internal circulation system needs water before the pump runs. Running it dry can damage it.

settings.text: Keep both flow controls closed initially.
settings.detail: Leave KRYO’s water-flow control and the Halo flow adjuster closed at this stage.

settings.text: Switch KRYO on.
settings.detail: Confirm the internal light turns on.

settings.text: Confirm normal circulation.
settings.detail: Listen for smooth circulation. A harsh dry-running sound means switch KRYO off immediately and add water.

settings.text: Continue filling slowly.
settings.detail: Keep the internal light on so you can see the level clearly as it rises.

settings.text: Stop below the upper internal and electrical area.
settings.detail: Do not overfill and never let water reach the upper internal area.

settings.text: Dry the top.
settings.detail: Wipe away any spills and dry the top surface before refitting the plug.

settings.text: Refit the fill plug.
settings.detail: Insert the supplied plug and confirm it sits correctly.

settings.text: Set approximately 15°C for first use.
settings.detail: Press SET and choose approximately 15°C. Lower the temperature gradually only after you know how your body responds.

settings.title: First session
settings.purpose: Start gently and learn the correct body position.
settings.critical:
START WITH YOUR BACK TO THE HALO

Do not start facing the Halo. Do not let the first water hit your face or chest.
settings.detail:
Sudden cold may cause an involuntary gasp and rapid breathing.

Do not hyperventilate, hold your breath or perform extreme breathwork.

Final check before you start.

  • Rear airflow is clear
  • The rail is secure
  • The hose is not kinked
  • Both seals are fitted
  • The PSU is dry and outside the splash zone
  • Water is below the maximum level
  • The starting temperature is around 15°C

Why position matters. The Halo balances coverage, flow and droplet size to create a film of cold water over the upper body. Positioning it above your head helps water spread across the shoulders and carry heat away from more skin. KRYO is a different experience from full-body immersion — a short, very cold session can still feel extremely powerful.

Controlling intensity. Lower flow — around 5 L/min — is gentler, cools more slowly and makes the reservoir last longer. Higher flow, around 8 to 10 L/min, is more intense and uses the reservoir much faster. Flow values remain configurable pending final production validation.

After your session. Close the Halo flow adjuster, switch off the water flow and check the remaining water level. Top up when needed, wipe splash from the display and power side, check connections for drips and keep rear airflow clear.
settings.always_visible:
• Chest pain, pressure or tightness
  • Severe breathlessness
  • Dizziness or faintness
  • Confusion
  • Loss of coordination
  • Uncontrolled shivering
  • Racing or irregular heartbeat
  • Panic or loss of breathing control
settings.alt_1: First session position: stand with your back to the Halo so the first water hits the upper back and shoulders, never the face or chest

settings.text: Start with your back to the Halo.
settings.detail: The first water should land across the upper back and shoulders, never the face or chest.

settings.text: Start warmer and at a lower flow.
settings.detail: Lower flow is gentler and makes the reservoir last longer. Flow values remain configurable pending final production validation.

settings.text: Breathe normally.
settings.detail: Do not hyperventilate, hold your breath or perform extreme breathwork.

settings.text: Rotate gradually only after breathing is controlled.
settings.detail: There is no need to rush the rotation. End the session immediately if you feel unwell.
